ns2:section.sectionText: What can music tell us about the nature of late and post-socialism in the newly independent Balkan states? How does music reflect the impact of state socialism, glasnost, perestroika, regime change, ethnic nationalism, conflict, new capitalist markets, displaced populations, and EU politics among southern Balkan communities and their neighbors? This course represents an intensive survey of musical life in Bulgaria, Macedonia, and Romania, paying particular attention to how politics, ethnicity, nationalism, gender, religion, and changing senses of place and belonging have influenced musical and folkloric developments since the mid-nineteenth century. Topics will include regional instruments, vocal polyphonies, and ensembles in village, socialist, and post-socialist contexts; contemporary popular culture; pre-socialist village customs, rituals, and their contemporary festivalization; the musical life of regional minorities; and much more. Musical styles of Greece and Turkey will also be considered wherever pertinent. Course materials will include key ethnographic monographs and journal articles; films, music videos, and audio recordings; as well as the instructor’s own research.
